curation.lead:
The Humpty Dumpty Institute (HDI) is a New York nonprofit incorporated on October 19, 1998 (NY Corp #2307873, EIN 13-4028567), originally registered at the Central Park West apartment of co-founder Michael W. Sonnenfeldt, according to review of corporate filings and 990 records [Finding #120]. Its stated mission — organizing Congressional Delegations (CODELs) and facilitating dialogue between U.S. lawmakers and foreign governments — placed it at the center of overlapping influence channels documented in the Jeffrey Epstein files. Mark Epstein, Jeffrey’s brother, served on the HDI board, signed its 2015 IRS 990 return, loaned the organization over $100,000 in 2014, and personally participated in first-class delegations to Bahrain and Azerbaijan, as records show [Finding #120][EFTA02598877]. When delegation slots opened on a May 2014 trip to Baku, Mark forwarded the recruitment email directly to Jeffrey, offering him the ability to place people from “media, finance, banking, education” on a Congressional delegation that would meet Azerbaijan’s president [EFTA02718091].

Analysis of records indicates HDI organized 52 or more CODELs to over 30 countries, hosting 250+ Members of Congress and 400+ senior staffers [Finding #130]. Its Congressional Advisory Board included 33 current and former lawmakers spanning both parties. Examination of public records shows that in August 2017 HDI formalized a partnership with Beijing’s Taihe Institute, a think tank whose senior fellows include 12 or more current and former CCP and PLA members [Finding #122]. Records indicate the partnership drew media scrutiny and Congressional resignations from the HDI advisory board, yet HDI maintained the relationship through at least the September 2019 Taihe Civilizations Forum in Beijing [Finding #124].

Analysis of FARA and LDA filings shows HDI has zero FARA registrations and zero lobbying filings in Senate LDA records [Finding #1150], despite its Taihe partnership and its role as the largest private CODEL organizer in the country. Comparable organizations — such as the China-United States Exchange Foundation — have registered under FARA with multiple registrants. Review of 990 filings shows HDI’s revenue declined over 80% from a peak of $1.82 million in 2011 to under $200,000 by 2018, with a partial recovery to $221,000 by 2023 [Finding #120][990:134028567].

sections.title: Key Relationships
sections.content:
The central relationship is with Jeffrey Epstein, mediated through his brother Mark Epstein. Records show Mark served as an HDI director, signed the 2015 IRS 990 return as “Mark L. Epstein, Director,” loaned the organization over $100,000 in 2014, and participated in CODELs to Bahrain (2013) and Azerbaijan (2014) [Finding #120][EFTA02598877]. In a December 22, 2014 email, Mark wrote to Jeffrey: “We (Humpty Dumpty Institute) led a congressional delegation to Bahrain to meet with ministers and the president (king/head poobah), opposition leaders, senate, head of the US Navy 5th fleet (headquartered in Bahrain) etc.” [EFTA02598877]. He added: “I did not know you were doing this kind of stuff. I was also on one to Azerbaijan, and might go on one to Turkey/Cypress in March.” The phrasing “I did not know you were doing this kind of stuff” implies Jeffrey had separate involvement in similar diplomatic-access activities.

According to records, Amir Dossal, former United Nations Chief of Partnerships and chairman of the Global Partnership Forum, served as an ex officio director of HDI [Finding #130]. On June 20, 2013, Dossal co-hosted a UN event on oceans and Sustainable Development Goals alongside Ghislaine Maxwell (representing the TerraMar Project) and Stuart Beck, Palau’s ambassador [Finding #114]. This placed an HDI director in direct programmatic collaboration with Maxwell at the United Nations. In August 2011, Dossal appeared alongside Deutsche Bank Global Head of Asset Management Kevin Parker and Russian Duma member Ilya Ponomarev at the New York Academy of Sciences “Science & the City Gala,” which honored UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon and featured James Simons, James Watson, and Jack Rosen [Finding #114].

Review of the 2015 990 filing shows the HDI board was a 14-member body chaired by Dr. Al Khalafalla, with chairman emeriti Constance Milstein (later a Biden ambassador nominee to Malta) and Sonnenfeldt [Finding #120][990:134028567]. Other directors included William J. Rouhana Jr. (co-founder and chairman since 2010, CEO of Chicken Soup for the Soul Entertainment), former Congressman Benjamin Gilman, Walter Arbib (SkyLink Group president), and Jay T. Snyder (HBJ Investments). The co-founder and president since 1998, Ralph L. Cwerman, drew $145,458 in annual compensation. Executive Director Joseph Merante, a former State Department Foreign Service officer, managed the CODEL operations and served as the point of contact for delegation logistics and the Taihe partnership.

sections.title: The Congressional Delegation
sections.content:
HDI’s core operational activity is the organization of private Congressional Delegations. Analysis of records indicates HDI organized 52 or more CODELs to over 30 countries over two decades, hosting more than 250 Members of Congress and 400 senior Congressional staff members [Finding #130]. Destinations have included Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Turkey, Cyprus, and UN headquarters in New York. The delegations are fully funded and “entirely first class with all first class accommodations,” according to CODEL recruitment emails found in Epstein’s files [EFTA02718091].

The mechanics of the CODEL operation are documented in detail through the May 2014 Azerbaijan delegation. When participants dropped out, HDI Executive Director Joseph Merante emailed seeking replacements from “media, finance, banking, education.” Mark Epstein forwarded Merante’s email directly to Jeffrey Epstein on May 22, 2014, writing: “In case you know someone and want to do them a favor: (let me know)” [EFTA02718091]. The full agenda, recovered from Epstein’s document files, lists meetings with President Ilham Aliyev, U.S. Ambassador Richard Morningstar, Foreign Affairs Minister Elmar Mammadyarov, and parliamentary committees [EFTA02725237]. The delegation provided face-to-face access to a head of state, and Jeffrey Epstein was offered the ability to fill empty seats.

Examination of records shows the Congressional Advisory Board, as constituted around 2022, included 33 or more current and former members of Congress from both parties: Don Bacon (R-NE), Andre Carson (D-IN), Judy Chu (D-CA), Jim Clyburn (D-SC), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Andy Harris (R-MD), Jim Himes (D-CT), Gregory Meeks (D-NY), Bennie Thompson (D-MS), Maxine Waters (D-CA), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL), and others [Finding #130]. Former advisory board members include Mark Meadows, Adam Schiff, and Sheila Jackson Lee. This bipartisan Congressional roster provided institutional credibility that preceded the Taihe Institute partnership.

sections.title: The Taihe Institute Partnership and CCP Nexus
sections.content:
In August 2017, HDI formalized a partnership with the Beijing-based Taihe Institute, a think tank whose senior fellows include 12 or more current and former members of the Chinese Communist Party and the People’s Liberation Army [Finding #122]. HDI Executive Director Merante participated in the Taihe Civilizations Forum in Beijing in both August 2017 and September 2019 [Finding #124]. Ruby Wang, Senior Vice President at Perfect World (a Chinese gaming company) and a Taihe fellow, joined the HDI board, connecting the two organizations at the governance level.

The partnership drew scrutiny from media and Congress. The Washington Examiner reported on HDI’s CCP connections, and multiple members of Congress resigned from the Advisory Board [Finding #124]. Taihe co-authored a report with HDI-adjacent figures that called the United States a “failed country” and promoted the claim that COVID-19 leaked from a Maryland military base. HDI stated publicly that it “never accepted any funds from the Taihe Institute or any Chinese Government organ or entity.” Under 22 USC 611(c), however, FARA’s definition of “agent of a foreign principal” does not require direct funding — acting “at the order, request, or under the direction or control” of a foreign principal is sufficient.

HDI thus operated simultaneously as the largest private CODEL organizer in the country, a formal partner of a CCP/PLA-linked think tank, and a board seat for an Epstein family member — all with zero FARA registrations and zero LDA lobbying filings [Finding #1150]. The China-United States Exchange Foundation, conducting comparable China-U.S. influence activities, registered under FARA with four separate registrants (Capitol Counsel #6328, Wilson Global #6584, BLJ Worldwide #5875, BGR Government Affairs #5430) [Finding #1150]. HDI’s functionally equivalent activities remain unregistered.

sections.title: Financial Profile and Contraction
sections.content:
Analysis of HDI’s IRS 990 filings shows a steep financial decline [Finding #120][990:134028567]. Revenue peaked at $1.82 million in 2011, sustained at $1.64 million (2012) and $1.70 million (2013), then fell: $1.47 million (2015), $481,000 (2016), $401,000 (2017), $227,000 (2018). A brief spike to $360,000 in 2019 was followed by continued decline: $202,000 (2020), $155,000 (2021), $174,000 (2022), and $221,000 (2023). Total assets peaked at $287,000 in 2011 and stood at $170,000 in 2023. This represents over 80% revenue decline from peak to trough.

Records indicate Mark Epstein loaned HDI over $100,000 in 2014 — a personal loan from a board director to the organization he governed [Finding #120]. The 2015 return, signed by Mark Epstein as director, flagged “Yes” on Line 25a (excess benefit transaction with a disqualified person) and Line 5a (party to a prohibited tax shelter transaction), and disclosed foreign bank accounts [990:134028567]. These disclosures rarely appear on nonprofit filings, individually or in combination.

The revenue trajectory parallels — at smaller scale — the decline at IPI, whose assets fell 73% from $12.6 million to $3.9 million over a similar period. Both organizations connect to the Epstein network through different pathways: HDI through Mark Epstein and Dossal; IPI through Terje Rod-Larsen and Gratitude America. The partial revenue recovery in 2022–2023 may reflect new funding sources, but without granular donor data from the 990s, the source cannot be determined.

sections.title: Regulatory Gaps and Disclosure Failures
sections.content:
HDI has zero FARA registrations despite its partnership with the CCP-linked Taihe Institute and its role facilitating meetings between U.S. lawmakers and foreign heads of state including Azerbaijan’s President Aliyev [Finding #1150]. It has zero lobbying filings in Senate LDA records despite maintaining a 33-member Congressional Advisory Board and organizing 52 or more CODELs [Finding #1150]. An organization with documented CCP institutional ties and Epstein family involvement in its governance has operated the country’s largest private Congressional delegation program entirely outside federal transparency requirements.

Under 22 USC 611(c), the definition of “agent of a foreign principal” encompasses anyone who acts “at the order, request, or under the direction or control” of a foreign principal. HDI’s Taihe partnership involved joint events, shared speakers, and co-produced publications — activities that, when performed by other organizations with Chinese government connections, have triggered FARA registration [Finding #1150]. HDI’s stated position — that it received no funds from Taihe or any Chinese government entity — addresses only the funding prong and does not resolve whether the partnership constitutes direction, control, or agent-of status under the broader statutory framework.

The 990 filing disclosures add further context. Review of the 2015 return shows it flagged excess benefit transactions, prohibited tax shelter participation, and foreign bank accounts, and was signed by Mark Epstein — the board member through whom Jeffrey Epstein was offered the ability to place individuals on Congressional delegations [Finding #120][EFTA02718091][990:134028567]. No public record of DOJ National Security Division review or Congressional inquiry into HDI’s FARA status has been identified.

open_questions: Who did Jeffrey Epstein place (or attempt to place) on HDI Congressional Delegations after Mark forwarded the May 2014 recruitment email? Were there other instances of delegation slot-filling beyond the documented Azerbaijan trip?

What is the full scope of the Taihe Institute partnership — were there memoranda of understanding, joint funding arrangements, or coordinated lobbying activities beyond the documented forum appearances and co-produced publications?
What explains the 2015 990 flags for excess benefit transactions and prohibited tax shelter participation? Who was the disqualified person, and what was the nature of the tax shelter?
Who funded HDI during its revenue collapse from $1.82M (2011) to under $200K (2018), and what accounts for the partial recovery in 2022–2023?
What role did Robert Lawrence Kuhn — who operates at the intersection of U.S.-China influence and Epstein-adjacent networks — play in relation to HDI or Taihe?
